questiontext.text:
ABCDEFGH is a cuboid. ABCD is the base, and E, F, G and H are vertically above A, B, C and D. For each pair of lines, choose whether they are parallel, intersecting or skew.

[[jsxgraph width="360px" height="280px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-1.2, 6.2, 8.9, -1.6], axis: false, grid: false, keepaspectratio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); // oblique projection: receding edges at 30 degrees, half length function P(x, y, z) { return [x + 0.5*y*Math.cos(Math.PI/6), z + 0.5*y*Math.sin(Math.PI/6)]; } var solid = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var hid = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var dot = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var tx = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 15, anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle'}; var cx = 3.87, cy = 2.0; function lab(Q, s) { var dx = Q[0]-cx, dy = Q[1]-cy, r = Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy) || 1; b.create('text', [Q[0]+0.42*dx/r, Q[1]+0.42*dy/r, s], tx); } function seg(Q, R, o) { b.create('segment', [Q, R], o); } function mark(Q, R, S) { // right-angle mark at Q between QR and QS function u(X) { var dx = X[0]-Q[0], dy = X[1]-Q[1], r = Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); return [0.3*dx/r, 0.3*dy/r]; } var a = u(R), c = u(S); b.create('polygon', [[Q[0]+a[0], Q[1]+a[1]], [Q[0]+a[0]+c[0], Q[1]+a[1]+c[1]], [Q[0]+c[0], Q[1]+c[1]]], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fillOpacity: 0, vertices: {visible: false}, borders: {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}}); } // cuboid ABCDEFGH: l = 6, w = 4, h = 3 (shape only) var A = P(0,0,0), B = P(6,0,0), C = P(6,4,0), D = P(0,4,0), E = P(0,0,3), F = P(6,0,3), G = P(6,4,3), H = P(0,4,3); seg(A,B,solid); seg(B,C,solid); seg(B,F,solid); seg(C,G,solid); seg(A,E,solid); seg(E,F,solid); seg(F,G,solid); seg(G,H,solid); seg(H,E,solid); // hidden corner D: its three edges dashed seg(A,D,hid); seg(D,C,hid); seg(D,H,hid); lab(A,'A'); lab(B,'B'); lab(C,'C'); lab(D,'D'); lab(E,'E'); lab(F,'F'); lab(G,'G'); lab(H,'H'); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
Two lines in space are parallel (same direction, never meet), intersecting (meet at one point) or skew (never meet and not parallel: no flat surface holds both).

  • {@PP[1][4]@}
  • {@PP[2][4]@}
  • {@PP[3][4]@}
  • {@PP[4][4]@}

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: parallel, intersecting or skew lines

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Classify pairs of edges and diagonals of a cuboid as parallel, intersecting or skew.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 13, Section 2.5 (parallel, intersecting and skew lines, Figure 8(a)) of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: new pairs of lines and our wording, four pairs per variant from a checked list of ten, as a classification question with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="kp1"]]

You chose parallel. Parallel lines point in the same direction, so one could be slid onto the other without turning it. {@PP[1][1]@} and {@PP[1][2]@} point in different directions, so that cannot be done here. Now decide: do they meet at a point, or do they miss each other?

[[else]][[if test="ki1"]]

You chose intersecting. Intersecting lines share a point, but {@PP[1][1]@} and {@PP[1][2]@} have no point in common, however far you extend them. Now compare their directions: the same, or different?

[[else]]

You chose skew. Skew lines pass two tests: they never meet, and they point in different directions. {@PP[1][1]@} and {@PP[1][2]@} fail one of these tests. Check each test on the diagram.
